espn-604003.headline: Jake White wants Ireland in Suva. First, Dublin
beats: Fiji hired the 2007 World Cup-winning coach last month, reportedly ahead of Warren Gatland and Shaun Edwards. He has used the week to invite Ireland to the Pacific, saying "There'd be nothing greater than for Fiji to host Ireland in Suva".

The invitation arrives with a 54–17 loss in Lyon to an injury-hit France and no points from four Nations Championship games. Ireland put six tries past Argentina last weekend. Andy Farrell's seven changes include Jamison Gibson-Park restored at scrum-half, and look more like maintenance than experiment.
White has brought Gert Smal, Ireland's forwards coach in the 2009 Grand Slam, so the visitors know the building. A Fiji win would drop Ireland to fifth, below France and England.
What Ireland want is a dominant bonus-point win with nobody hurt, because South Africa come to Dublin next. White knows a little about them too.

espn-604004.headline: Both know 21–43 by heart. Only one keeps sixth
beats: Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield last weekend, the same score they took away to Ireland in March. Australia lost 21–43 to New Zealand in October, and have since added 22–45 at Twickenham.

Ewan Ashman scored a hat-trick against New Zealand, then Scotland failed to score in the second half. Australia have conceded 50, 43 and 45 in their last three. Neither defence arrives with references.
Scotland won the last Test between them 27–13 in 2024. Their Australia-born captain, Sione Tuipulotu, says he has "that little bit of fire bubbling away whenever I play against the Wallabies".
An Australia win would take sixth in the world off Scotland. With Japan and Wales to come six days later, the loser gets less than a week to find a tackle.

espn-604005.headline: New Zealand need more than revenge to get back to 1st
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. New Zealand were 1st in the world until 31 August, and only a win by 16 or more puts them back above South Africa.

Both arrive on three straight wins. New Zealand have scored 43, 50 and 43 since South Africa put 43 on them in September. England's 45 against Australia was the most they have ever scored against them, and it came after headlines over an alleged rift in camp and eased the pressure on Steve Borthwick.
England have been 5th in every ranking since July, which is about how steady a side can look while being told it is falling apart.
New Zealand's next game after this is Chile at the World Cup, in October. Whatever the margin here, they will have a long time to think about it.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland score freely. So does everyone they play
beats: Scotland scored seven tries against Argentina in July and still conceded 38. New Zealand put 43 past them at Murrayfield on 7 November, the same total Ireland managed in March.

Japan lost 28–21 to Wales in Cardiff the same day, a seven-point game away from home. Eddie Jones then promised his youthful side would "play the house down" at Twickenham, which is not a defensive plan.
A Japan win drops Scotland below Australia in the world rankings, the side Scotland host at Murrayfield the weekend before.
Win, and Scotland's next problem is Italy in February. Lose, and they get the winter to work out where the 43s keep coming from.

espn-604007.headline: Ireland's scrum has had a year to think about Dublin
beats: South Africa won 24–13 at the Aviva last November, and the scrum did most of it: six penalties from 16 scrums, a penalty try, and Ireland penalised ten times in the 12 that were not reset. Five Irish players were carded, James Ryan among them with a 20-minute red.

Andrew Porter was one of the yellows. Calf problems then kept him out of the Six Nations and the summer tour, which left that night as his last Test going into this month. His approach to the rematch is "Swing at it".

South Africa arrive off a 21–19 defeat in Paris. Ireland put six tries past Argentina in a 42–12 win. A home win would knock the world champions off the top of the rankings, with New Zealand the ones moving up.
Ireland have spent the autumn promising more fitness and better hands. This one asks about the front row first.

espn-604008.headline: Italy are one win from 9th. They have none yet
beats: The bottom two of the Nations Championship meet in Udine with nine games and no wins between them. Fiji sit two places higher in the world, and that gap is what this game decides.

Italy conceded 66 at home to South Africa and 57 in Australia. Beat Fiji and they go up to 9th, above Fiji and Wales, which is a long way to climb for a side that has not scored more than 17 in its last five Tests.

Fiji shipped 54 in France, but a fortnight earlier they won 34–28 in Japan. Jake White, who took South Africa to the 2007 World Cup, started the job last month with his eye on next year's World Cup in Australia.
Neither side plays again until February at the earliest, so the loser keeps this one all winter.

espn-604009.headline: Even a draw costs France fourth place
beats: France have been fourth in the world since 13 July. Argentina have won once in 2026. That gap is why anything short of a French win in Saint-Denis lets England past them.
France beat South Africa 21–19 last week, a week after putting 54 points on Fiji. They are short-handed, with options at 10 thinned out this autumn, though a playmaker is back in time for this.

Argentina lost 42–12 in Ireland. Their year also includes three defeats and a draw in Buenos Aires. A squad built mostly from Top 14 players now meets the side most of them face on a Saturday at home. France won the last meeting 37–23, in November 2024.
France's next game is Wales in February. Argentina's next after this is Canada at the World Cup, which leaves them a long time to think about Paris.

espn-604010.headline: Australia have let in 138 in three Tests. Now Cardiff
beats: New Zealand put 50 and 43 on Australia in October. Away to England on 8 November, they conceded 45 more. Their last win was 42–38 over South Africa in September, which proves the attack exists and says little about the defence.
The answer to the England defeat is Carter Gordon and Rob Valetini back in the starting XV, with Meredith dropped from the match-day 23. The brief is avoiding a fourth straight loss.
Wales beat Japan 28–21 on 7 November with four tries. They are also the side that went to South Africa in July and lost 43–0. Win this, and they climb to ninth in the world.
Wales go to France in February. Australia's next game is Hong Kong at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to sit with a fourth defeat.
